sam: Heads-up — I found a reproducible memory growth pattern in the KV cache during long-context runs that shows up differently on Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private. On Dedicated we see paging spikes and frequent evictions after ~30m of steady traffic. Repro steps below. Anyone seen this?

maria: I saw something similar on the perf harness last Thursday. Dedicated pools using older drivers + kernel 5.15 had more pagefault churn when the KV backfill kicked in.

cheng: Can you paste the vmstat / proc output around the spike? Also which jemalloc version and LD_PRELOAD are you using?

sam: here's a trimmed snippet from the Dedicated run where the plateau turns into growth:```
procs -----------memory---------- ---swap-- -----io---- -system-- ------cpu-----
 r  b   swpd   free   buff  cache   si   so    bi    bo   in   cs us sy id wa st
 1  0      0  1024M   32M  8200M    0    0   1200   3400  1200 4000 10  2 85  3  0
... (spike at +00:30)
pgfaults: 5.2k -> 42k in 5m
kv_reclaim_count: 3 -> 87
kv_frag_ratio: 0.12 -> 0.47
```
Config used:
```
LD_PRELOAD=/opt/jemalloc/lib/libjemalloc.so MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:true,lg_dirty_mult:2
vm.swappiness=60
thp=always
```

infra-bot: infra-bot: canary deploy for test-run-339 completed on dedicated-gpu-pool-3. Logs uploaded to s3://perf-uploads/3391234567/. CI job id: perf-339.

oliver: Hypothesis: the combination of jemalloc background threads + high swappiness + THP compaction is increasing fragmentation and causing the kernel to reclaim pages more aggressively on our Dedicated images (older kernel + driver). On on-prem A100s the NVLINK mappings make page compaction heavier. Try disabling jemalloc bg thread and reduce swappiness to 10. Also try a smaller batch window to avoid prolonged KV backfill bursts.

nina: I ran a quick A-B: Dedicated instance pinned to kernel 6.2, vm.swappiness=10, jemalloc bg disabled. Longctx (64k tokens) run for 45m: page reclaim events dropped ~30% and kv_frag_ratio plateaued at 0.18. p50 latency increased ~3ms. Uploading traces to the same bucket.

cheng: Interesting — could be kernel THP compaction + cma/mmap behavior. Can you also try `echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled` (thp=never) and rerun? The compaction path in 5.x vs 6.x handles scattered GPU mappings differently.

sam: did the thp=never + jemalloc bg disabled + swappiness=10 run just now. Longctx 64k tokens, 90% load. Result: background evictions almost disappeared, KV memory plateaued after warmup. No spike in pgfaults. Looks like a combinatorial interaction rather than a single root cause.

maria: Good catch. Action items: formalize these permutations into a small matrix for perf CI (kernel versions, thp policy, swappiness, jemalloc bg on/off, batch size). Add kv_reclaim_count and kv_frag_ratio as first-class metrics and alert on sustained growth. I'll open a ticket with steps + links to traces.

sam: Thanks. Question: should we change the Dedicated default image to vm.swappiness=10 and thp=never? @infra-bot / @oliver thoughts on rollout risk.

infra-bot: infra-bot: infra-runbook: https://redwood.internal/infra/runbooks/kv-frag. Canary rollout tool queued.

oliver: I'd prefer a conservative, Dedicated-only change rolled via canary with telemetry. Hosted customers have diverse workloads; changing THP/swappiness cluster-wide could have side effects. I'll draft a rollout plan: 10% Dedicated pools -> monitor kv_reclaim_count / p99 mem pressure for 48h -> expand. Also propose adding a targeted batching tweak (reduce batch window by 20%) as a config knob to reduce sustained backfill pressure.

nina: I'll add the experiments to the perf matrix and schedule nightly runs across Dedicated/Hosted/Private images. We'll capture driver/kernel combos and generate a short summary doc.

sam: Excellent. I'll attach the exact repro script below and link the perf traces in the ticket. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

--- repro (quick) ---
1) start perf harness with longctx profile (64k tokens, parallel 8)
2) env: LD_PRELOAD=... jemalloc bg true/false, vm.swappiness=10/60, thp=always/never, kernel 5.15/6.2
3) capture /proc/vmstat, `perf record -e page-faults` and kv metrics every 30s
4) analyze: look for sustained increase in kv_frag_ratio and kv_reclaim_count vs baseline

If anyone wants I can paste the full perf diff in here or link the S3 traces.
